what was found: *** Catedral Basilica San Jose, Religious Marriage Records March 1825-September 1859 ***, DGS film 008143329 (microfilm 625330), image 87, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-67KL: "En esta Parroquia de San Jose a tres de Febrero de mil ochocientos treinta y siete... Don *** MAURICIO LERENA, natural de la VILLA DEL COLLA, hijo legitimo de Don RAMON y de Dona MARIA GONZALEZ ***, con *** Dona CASIMIRA MONTANO, natural de esta Villa, hija legitima de Don JOSE y Dona IGNACIA BARREDO ***". Teniente de cura Fray Froylan Mellid; certified Jose Joaquin Reyna; witnesses Don Vicente Muniz and Dona Clara Ledena.
what it does to the argument: *** THE INDEX WAS RIGHT AND THE ARGUMENT BUILT ON IT WAS WRONG. *** The act names Ramon and Maria Gonzalez exactly as the index did - *** and it says Mauricio was born at COLLA ***, where the 1858 expediente calls the Trinidad Lerenas *** naturales de SAN JOSE ***. *** SO THE 'SHARED PLACE OF ORIGIN' PUBLISHED THAT MORNING IS WITHDRAWN. *** He married at San Jose; they were born there. *** THE INDEX FIELD SAID 'Birthplace: Colla' ON THE VERY PAGE BEING CITED. ***

the step: *** AND A WITNESS WHO IS NOT CLAIMED ***
what was found: "fueron testigos de su Otorgamiento Don *** Vicente Muniz *** y Dona *** CLARA LEDENA ***"
what it does to the argument: *** LEDENA IS WHAT THE PLATE SAYS, AND LEDENA IS WHAT IS RECORDED. *** The temptation is obvious - a woman of almost the right surname standing at Mauricio's wedding - and this archive has eleven documented cases of LERENA written as something else. *** BUT THE LETTERFORM IS NOT THE ONE: *** the fourth character carries a tall ascender where 'Lerena' four lines above has a plain shoulder. *** A TRAP THIS ARCHIVE IS PRONE TO IS NOT A LICENCE TO SEE IT EVERYWHERE. ***

the step: *** THE REPLACEMENT ARGUMENT, AND IT IS A BETTER ONE ***
what was found: *** Flores. Birth Records 1887-1902 ***, act No. 8 of *** 2 March 1895 *** at El Tala, image 165, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-334D-Z: *** Don CIPRIANO LERENA, forty-two, hacendado ***, registers his daughter *** CARMEN DONATA ***, names his wife *** Dona LAUREANA BELOQUI, thirty-nine ***, and gives the child's paternal grandparents as *** MAURICIO, oriental, FALLECIDO, y CASIMIRA MONTANO de setenta y cuatro anos, VIUDA, domiciliada en la ciudad SAN JOSE DE MAYO, CALLE ARENAL NUMERO 240 ***
what it does to the argument: *** CIPRIANO LERENA OF TRINIDAD IS A SON OF MAURICIO LERENA OF COLLA. *** This register has carried him since 13 September as 'one of the men fathering Lerena children at Trinidad in the 1870s and 1880s' with a wife Lauriana Beloqui - and separately, since 21 September, as an index-only 'Cipriano LERENA Montana' whose 1928 death registration named Mauricio and Casimira. *** ONE ACT NAMES THE WIFE AND BOTH PARENTS, SO THE ROWS ARE MERGED. ***

what was found: Bernabe of Trinidad is a grandson of a *** RAMON LERENA and MARIA GONZALEZ *** by the kinship schema of 1858. Cipriano of Trinidad is a grandson of a *** RAMON LERENA and MARIA GONZALEZ *** by the 1837 act and the 1895 act together.
what it does to the argument: *** TWO OF THE SIX OR SEVEN TRINIDAD MEN DESCEND FROM THAT COUPLE, BY TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES THAT SHARE NO DOCUMENT. *** *** AND THE 'STILL NOT PROOF, NOT MERGED' THIS CELL ORIGINALLY CARRIED IS WITHDRAWN ON BOTH COUNTS. *** First because *** THIS ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY MADE THE IDENTIFICATION ON 17 SEPTEMBER *** in data/ramon-lerena-rosario.tsv, which the author of this file had not read. Second because *** THE 1825 MARRIAGE ACT WAS READ OFF THE PLATE THE SAME AFTERNOON ***: Alejandro Lereña, *** natural de la Villa del ROSARIO, hijo legitimo de RAMON LEREÑA y de MARIA JOSEFA GONZALEZ ***. *** THE CAUTION WAS NOT WRONG AS A HABIT - IT WAS WRONG AS A FACT, AND IT COST A DAY OF SAYING LESS THAN THE ARCHIVE KNEW. ***

the step: *** AND CASIMIRA MONTANO STOPS BEING A NAME ***
what was found: Seventy-four in March 1895, a *** widow ***, living at *** Calle Arenal 240, San Jose de Mayo ***; and on 7 August 1850 she buried a daughter of seven days, *** ABDONA IGNACIA ***, '*** en el angelorio ***' at the Parroquia de San Jose (Religious Death Records 1839-1851, image 94)
what it does to the argument: *** BORN ABOUT 1821, AND STILL AT SAN JOSE DE MAYO FIFTY-EIGHT YEARS AFTER SHE MARRIED THERE. *** *** IT ALSO DATES MAURICIO'S DEATH: *** he is fallecido by March 1895. *** AND THE DEAD INFANT CARRIES HER GRANDMOTHER'S NAME, IGNACIA BARREDO *** - which is a warning as much as a fact: row 319 lists an *** Ignacia Lerena marrying at Trinidad in 1882 *** as a candidate child of this couple, and reusing a dead infant's name was ordinary. *** THAT IS EXACTLY HOW TWO PEOPLE BECOME ONE BY ACCIDENT. ***

the step: *** AND A SECOND MAURICIO, SEPARATED BY ONE WORD ***
what was found: *** Flores. Death Records 1886-1887 ***, image 8, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-QHVC: a witness signing in his own hand, '*** D. MAURICIO LERENA de CINCUENTA anos de edad, oriental, casado, hacendado ***, vecino de esta Seccion'
what it does to the argument: *** THE TRANSCRIPT GARBLES THE AGE TO 'VEINCUENTA', WHICH IS NOT A WORD *** - and the age is the whole of what separates this man from the one who married in 1837. *** SO IT WAS READ OFF THE PLATE: CINCUENTA. *** Fifty in 1886 is a birth about *** 1836 ***, which is *** BEFORE *** that marriage. *** HE IS NOT ENTERED AS A SON ***: either the stated age is loose in the ordinary way, or they are not father and son. *** THE DISTINCTION IS CARRIED, NOT RESOLVED - AND IT IS CARRIED BECAUSE ONE WORD WAS CHECKED. ***
